task_message:
Case L42: segment the lipomatous soft-tissue tumor on this T1-weighted MRI.

Volume: 251x251x265 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
Case L42 is complete. 

**What I did:**
1. **Located the lesion** with overview + axial/coronal/sagittal contact sheets: a large, encapsulated fatty (T1-bright) mass in the deep soft tissues of the limb, with a thin dark capsule and a more heterogeneous, intermediate-signal solid component inferiorly, spanning axial slices ~40–232.
2. **Started the mask** with two positive points (marks 427, 488) inside the bright portion on axial slice 130 — the model produced a single 826 mL component whose boundary tracked the tumor's capsule in all three planes.
3. **Verified the extent**: checked the upper pole (axial 45/62), lower pole (axial 225/240), the past-the-end panels (axial 32/240, coronal 54/188, sagittal 40/130) — no clear tumor tissue beyond the mask ends, and no stray components.
4. **Refined** the boundary (v2, 807 mL, −23 mL / +4.5 mL vs v1) so it hugs the capsule smoothly.
5. **Rejected all intensity-based candidates**: C1–C3 were the normal subcutaneous fat ring around the limb, C4/C5 tiny (≈1 mL) fat lobules; none were tumor.

**Result:** final mask v2 — one component, 807.4 mL, extent axial 40–232, coronal 62–180, sagittal 48–130.

**Confidence: medium** — the main mass and its capsule are followed cleanly in all three planes, but a prominent honeycomb-fat area in the anterior subcutis superiorly is a separate structure from the tumor capsule, so I chose not to include it.
